name: Marketo
tagline: Enterprise marketing automation platform by Adobe.
description: Marketo is Adobe's enterprise marketing automation platform for nurture programs, lead scoring, and email and landing page construction.
pros: Programs hold segments, triggers, and success criteria together, so a campaign is a structure rather than a one-off send
Behavior-based scoring hands sales a ranked queue instead of a flat list of signups
Emails, landing pages, and forms are built in the same system as the nurture logic, removing handoffs between tools
Adobe ownership places documentation, contracting, and roadmap under one large vendor's processes
The band this dataset records, $895-3195/mo, gives a buyer a starting figure before any vendor conversation
cons: The recorded entry band sits above every email-led alternative in this repository's comparison set, which prices out first-tool buyers
Administration is a real job: scoring models, program structures, and list hygiene need an owner with dedicated time
No certification, retention term, or residency option shows up in this repository's fields for Marketo

content.title: The nurture program as Marketo's unit of work
content.body: Marketo is enterprise marketing automation, and the object it organizes is the nurture program: a sustained sequence of emails, content, and branch decisions that moves a person from first interest toward a sales-ready state. Campaigns are built as programs with segments, triggers, and success criteria rather than as one-off sends. This repository files Marketo under Marketing & SEO with a paid model and a band of $895-3195/mo, describes it as an enterprise marketing automation platform by Adobe, and its category notes place Marketo among the all-in-one marketing suites alongside HubSpot.

content.title: Lead scoring and the handoff to sales
content.body: Scoring is the mechanism that turns behavior into a routing decision: opens, visits, form fills, and downloads accumulate points against a model the organization defines, and a person crosses a threshold into the sales queue. The same model can demote contacts who have gone quiet, which keeps a database from filling with names nobody has heard from in a year. What this dataset does not record is which scoring actions ship by default, how attribution is handled, or how a score is meant to reconcile with sales's own judgment — the practical detail a marketing operations hire would ask for first.

content.title: Landing pages, emails, and program building
content.body: The construction surface covers the assets a campaign needs, and they are built next to the logic that uses them rather than exported into it. Triggers react to behavior as it happens rather than on a fixed send schedule, which is what separates automation from a newsletter tool. None of the specific editors, template counts, or form capabilities are itemized in this repository, so the depth question has to be put to the vendor directly. The through-line is that asset and logic live in one system, so a campaign change does not require moving between tools.
items: Emails built from templates and attached to a program
Landing pages with forms feeding the same audience lists
Lists and segments refreshed from attributes and behavior
Triggers that start a step when a person acts
Success criteria that define when a program step is won

content.title: Adobe ownership and what it changes
content.body: Marketo's ownership sits inside Adobe, and the buying conversation follows from that. Documentation, release cadence, support packaging, and roadmap run through a large vendor's processes; the website field recorded for Marketo in this dataset points at Adobe's business domain rather than a standalone company site. For a buyer, the practical questions concern how Marketo is packaged alongside other Adobe products, what contracting looks like through that channel, and how much of the roadmap is shared with the wider suite. This repository records none of those terms.

content.title: What Marketo will not solve
content.body: What Marketo does not do is the point of comparing it carefully. It is not an experimentation platform: it will not run A/B tests across a product surface or manage staged feature rollouts, which is Optimizely's problem rather than Marketo's. It is not a survey tool, so structured feedback collection belongs elsewhere — this repository pairs Marketo with SurveyMonkey on that axis. And it is not an entry-level purchase: the recorded band of $895-3195/mo sits above the bands this dataset holds for ActiveCampaign, Mailchimp, and ConvertKit, which makes it a difficult fit for a team buying its first marketing tool.

content.title: The $895-3195/mo record, read carefully
content.body: Read from the stored fields, Marketo is carried as a paid product with a band of $895-3195/mo — an entry figure near the top of the bands this repository holds for its marketing counterparts, and above every email-led alternative in the same comparison set. The field does not say whether the band is per instance, priced against contact volume, or charged per seat, nor which modules it includes. Everything in this page is read from Adobe's published Marketo documentation and the records this repository holds for the product, so the band should be treated as a stored reference and checked against the vendor's current published pricing.

content.title: An all-in-one suite's ecosystem, and the certification silence
content.body: Suite products are expected to carry their own integration surface rather than depend on a connector market: a documented API for programmatic access, connections to CRM and analytics systems, and a named position in this repository's wider dataset, where the analytics review lists Marketo as an integration target alongside Salesforce. On the security side the record is empty — no certification, retention term, residency option, or identity detail is stored for Marketo here, and none follows from Adobe ownership. Buyers should confirm both the current connector list and the compliance documentation directly.

content.title: Marketo next to Optimizely: two different problems
content.body: The comparison that matters most for this file is Marketo against Optimizely, and it is not a like-for-like contest: Marketo builds nurture programs and scores leads, while Optimizely runs experiments and staged releases across a site or a product. Both sit under Marketing & SEO here at 4.1/5, yet a team needing both would be buying two platforms for two jobs. The rest of Marketo's recorded comparison set is the email-led field — ActiveCampaign, Mailchimp, ConvertKit — plus HubSpot as the all-in-one suite and the SEO tools Ahrefs, Moz, and SEMrush, which solve a third problem.

content.title: Who Marketo is for
content.body: Marketo suits marketing operations teams with a real nurture program, a lead-handoff process with sales, and the staff to administer both — usually organizations where the recorded band is a small line against the revenue the program is expected to move. It also suits buyers already standardizing on Adobe tooling. It does not suit a small team buying its first email platform, a product team that needs experimentation rather than nurture, or a buyer whose security review must start from certification evidence, which this repository does not hold. The dataset carries 4.1/5 for Marketo across 1,840 recorded reviews.

faqs.question: What is Marketo's core unit of work?
faqs.answer: A nurture program: segmented audiences, scheduled or triggered email steps, and success criteria, with landing pages and forms feeding the same structure. That is how it differs from a standalone email tool.

faqs.question: How does Marketo differ from Optimizely?
faqs.answer: They solve different problems. Marketo runs nurture programs and lead scoring; Optimizely runs A/B tests and feature rollouts. This repository files both under Marketing & SEO at 4.1/5, but neither replaces the other.

faqs.question: Is Marketo owned by Adobe?
faqs.answer: Yes. This dataset's website field for Marketo points to Adobe's business domain, and the product is described here as an enterprise marketing automation platform by Adobe.

faqs.question: What does this repository record for Marketo's price?
faqs.answer: A paid model with a band of $895-3195/mo. What that band covers — per instance, per contact volume, or per seat — is not recorded, so confirm current published pricing with the vendor.

faqs.question: Are security certifications listed for Marketo?
faqs.answer: No. The certification, retention, residency, and identity entries for Marketo in this repository, so compliance questions must go to the vendor's current documentation.

author: Emily Nakamura
learningCurve: Sending is straightforward; program structure, scoring models, and attribution are learned over weeks of administration rather than hours.
whoShouldUse: Marketing operations teams running sustained nurture programs with a defined lead handoff to sales, organizations already buying through Adobe, and mid-to-large teams with the staff to administer scoring and program structure.
whoShouldNotUse: Small teams buying a first email platform, product teams that need experimentation rather than nurture, and buyers whose security review requires proof of certification this repository does not carry.
